title: Using `steps_per_epoch` with PyDataset with `use_multiprocessing=True` always runs out of data

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi @reporter -

Thanks for reporting this issue. I am also reproducing the issue. 
Here is the breakdown of all warnings and error for all backends.

**For JAX Backend:**
JAX support parallelize operation. So when running above code with JAX backend you can use use_multiprocessing=False. 
Find more details about [JAX parallelize](https://jax.readthedocs.io/en/latest/sharded-computation.html) operation here. 

**For Torch Backend:**
The warning your getting because MyDataset class doesn't have defined batch size. You can define size of data points and batch size in pydataset class using __init__ method and __len__method. Or also can use .repeat()  to repeat the dataset in training loops. 

**For Tensorflow Backend:**
Here the warning cause in tensorflow backend because you didn't define You can define size of data points and batch size in pydataset class using __init__ method and __len__method.

Here you can find more details about [pydataset class](https://keras.io/api/utils/python_utils/#pydataset-class) with example

**Torch backend GPU error:**
multiprocessing.pool.MaybeEncodingError and 'RuntimeError('_share_filename_: only available on CPU')'
This error is because of using multiprocessing on GPU. Because this is very simple code that can easily run on GPU. That doesn't require multiprocessing. 

**.repeat() function in all backend:**
Torch: 
```
x = torch.tensor([1, 2, 3])
x.repeat(4, 2)
```
Keras:
```
x = keras.Input(shape=(32,))
y = keras.layers.RepeatVector(3)(x)
```
JAX:
```
a = jnp.array([[1, 2],[3, 4]])
jnp.repeat(a, 2, axis=-1)
```

Let me know if you need further details. Thanks...!!!

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi @reporter - Apologies. 

Here For tensorflow backend, instead of giving use_multiprocessing argument `dataset = MyDataset(workers=1, use_multiprocessing=True)` inside MyDataset class generated from PyDataset Class, you can try to initialise multiprocessing first and then start spawn process. Spawn is the parent process starts a fresh Python interpreter process. The child process will only inherit those resources necessary to run the process object. 

And for torch backend, use DataLoader. DataLoader will use multiprocessing to load data in parallel.Data Loader has num_workers shows how many subprocesses to use for data loading.
And in the torch, you can also use multiprocessing like this.
Multiprocessing is set up by defining the number of processes to use and creating a list of processes.
model.share_memory() method helps to allocate shared memory for the model parameters so that they can be accessed by multiple processes. 

Here is the attached [gist](https://colab.sandbox.google.com/gist/participant1/296807a77602a80003b70f6eff4f1dd5/pydataset_multiprocessing.ipynb) is running fine on GPU with multiprocessing.

2. `UserWarning: Your input ran out of data`

The code suggested in https://github.com/keras-team/keras/issues/20032#issuecomment-2271460200 seems to be working with all backends and doesn't have the first problem (the training getting stuck)! Could you confirm that it's what you're looking for?

comments.author: reporter
participant1
comments.body:
Hi @reporter -

`UserWarning: Your input ran out of data` this warning comes because the model get exhausted with available data before completing defined the specified number of epochs or steps per epoch and this is because dataset generated is too small for training configuration. As mentioned in my earlier comment either increase the dataset using .repeat() function it will remove the warning or `steps_per_epoch=1` in https://github.com/keras-team/keras/issues/20032#issuecomment-2271460200. By setting `steps_per_epoch=1`, model processes exactly one batch per epoch, matching the data availability and preventing the out of data error.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hi @participant1

> this warning comes because the model get exhausted with available data before completing defined the specified number of epochs or steps per epoch and this is because dataset generated is too small for training 

This is incorrect. While the warning text may make it seem like this, you can try any arbitrarily large dataset, or an infinite dataset as in my original post. E.g., defining the following in your previously referenced gist still yields the warning when `use_multiprocessing=True`:

```py3
@property
def num_batches(self):
    return 999999999999
```

> increase the dataset using .repeat()

As I explained above, this is not necessary and not a fix.

> use `steps_per_epoch=1`

This is not a solution, since no sensible training routine will use a single step per epoch. Steps and epochs have delicate interplay due to other utilities such as learning rate scheduling, `on_epoch_end` callbacks, etc.


@participant4 @participant5 Perhaps one of you could provide some insight into the issue?

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
@reporter ,

The warning is indeed the visible manifestation of a bigger problem. It should continue going through the `PyDataset` epoch after epoch, but right now, it restarts it from the beginning instead.
I'm working on a fix.

Thanks!

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
@reporter ,

I have a PR up for the fix.

Note that for multiprocessing with a GPU (CUDA), you will need this like suggested:
```python
multiprocessing.set_start_method("spawn")
```
Now, I have to say that I could no reproduce the error you had with Torch on GPU. I would get the same warnings as without a GPU. I hope this still fixes it though.
